headline: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5 at about 75% lower cost
dek: The smallest Claude 5.5 model is live on Amazon Bedrock with a per-task effort control and a much lower price, according to AWS and SiliconANGLE.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A small model, priced to run at volume
body: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5, the smallest model in its Claude 5.5 family. Amazon has already switched it on in Amazon Bedrock and the Claude Platform on AWS (AWS Machine Learning, SiliconANGLE).

The target is subagent work, where a cheaper model takes tasks handed down by a larger one: routing coding requests, reviewing pull requests, bulk summaries, browser automation. Harder reasoning stays with Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 (AWS Machine Learning, SiliconANGLE).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Effort on a dial, work split by size
s3.body: Haiku 5.5 is the first Haiku with a tunable effort setting: each task can trade intelligence for speed and cost on its own (AWS Machine Learning, SiliconANGLE).

points.t: Each step of a pipeline picks its own level, instead of one setting forced across the whole chain (AWS Machine Learning).
Claude Opus 5.5, launched September 22, handles planning and the harder judgment calls (AWS Machine Learning).
The small model carries out work that is already well defined, at volume, as the cheaper worker (AWS Machine Learning).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Priced level with OpenAI's budget model
body: Prompts up to 100,000 tokens (the text units models bill by), which Anthropic says cover nine in ten Haiku 4.5 requests, now cost ten cents per million input tokens and fifty cents per million output, down from one and five dollars (SiliconANGLE).
That matches OpenAI's GPT-6 Luna. In Anthropic's own tests, Haiku 5.5 scored 72.4% on OSWorld 2.1, where agents run a real computer, against Luna's 48.9% (SiliconANGLE).

items.t: Cache-read pricing, the rate for reusing stored context, fell from twenty to ten cents per million tokens (SiliconANGLE).
Claude Max and Team subscribers start getting monthly API credit: $100 on Max 5x, double on Max 20x, up to $500 on Team (SiliconANGLE).
Beyond AWS, the model is live on Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure (SiliconANGLE).

caption.hook: Anthropic launched Claude Haiku 5.5, its smallest Claude 5.5 model, now on Amazon Bedrock at about 75% lower cost.
body: Asana ran Haiku 5.5 through the evaluation suite of its AI Teammates agent ahead of launch. Task completion latency dropped more than 30%, and each agent turn ran up to two and a half times faster, SiliconANGLE reports.

The comparison with GPT-6 Luna relies on benchmarks Anthropic picked and ran itself. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, a coding test, Haiku 5.5 reportedly scored 39.2% against 16.4%. Anthropic also estimates the Sonnet 5.5 cache cut trims about a fifth off most agentic workloads, per SiliconANGLE.
